newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas pares chart losses, still off late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas pares chart losses, still off late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared technical morning losses but remained mostly lower late Friday in quiet trade, still undermined by expectations that mild weather next week will pressure the early-June cash.
At 1405 EDT, spot-July was still down by two cents at $2.23 per million British thermal units after dipping to $2.20 early. August was 2.6 cents lower at $2.225.

"We saw a lot of selling early, but it's quiet now. I think we hit some sell stops this morning after we broke support, but we got some short covering this afternoon," said one New York-based futures trader.

While most traders were sidelined waiting for June flows to begin, some said they expected mild Midwest and Northeast weather next week to put the early-June cash on the defensive. But others said forecasts for more heat in the Southwest and steady injection demand should limit the slide.

Chart traders said July's break today of trendline support turned the technical picture more bearish. They pegged next support in the $2.17 area and then around $2.09. Resistance remained at $2.37-2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, June Gulf Coast prices notionally slipped by about five cents Friday to the low-$2.20s. June Midcon gas fell a similar amount to about $2.05. New York city gate prices lost a nickel or more to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 17,448 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
On KCBT, July eased 0.2 cent to $2.105, while deferreds were steady to one cent lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.8 cents to 12.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
